patches.reason: "You earned yourself a punish point." calls punish() without the count; Groovy passes null, and punish's 1..i loop fails on 1..null. Every other caller passes the points it announces; pass 1.

inform awards "5 punish points only for thinking about quitting" with punish(5), but unlike its sibling scripts it never defines punish, and script-local closures are not shared, so Groovy failed there. Add the same punish closure the sibling scripts define (sleep.groovy's null-safe form), in both retained versions.

eat's ben-wa-balls feedback raises or lowers chanceBenWaBalls and saves it as domme.chanceBenWaBalls, but only chores declares and loads that variable, so Groovy failed on the first ++/--. Load it at the top of eat as chores does, with the same default of 8 for a profile that has none yet (see chores-ben-wa-default).

SMinder ends its own story with return "Domme", return null and "End of the Script"; after that, two pasted copies of a Milovana tease (33003) redeclare endReached, block and newBlock at script level, which Groovy rejects ("The current scope already contains a variable"), so the script never compiled. Wrap the unreachable tail in a block comment; it contains no */ of its own.

chores reads domme.chanceBenWaBalls into an int, which fails on a fresh profile because nothing has saved the key yet (only chores and eat save it, and chores reads it first). Its next lines raise any value below 8 to 8 and save it, so 8 is the value the tease starts with: read into an Integer and default a missing key to 8.
